decisions.reason: Attributes the sole crash to plugin A's unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call, grounds it in the console stack trace and the alpha1→alpha2 contract diff showing the prop removed and replaced by useSessionStatus, and explicitly clears plugin B (no standard-kit hooks). Does not claim useSessions was removed.

Explains B's chips vanish because both dock entries mount under one shared input.dock DrawerErrorBoundary whose null fallback unmounts the whole subtree, cites the console fallback log and render tree, and explains the attach button's survival via the separate input.left boundary.

Reads the disable-A experiment as proving render-crash coupling and B's ability to render when freed; explicitly states it does not prove B is fully alpha.2-compatible nor that A is the only dock defect; explains reinstalling B was futile since B was never broken; falsifies the colleague's both-hit theory because B uses no standard-kit hooks.

Provides corrected component code reading pendingInteraction via useSessionStatus with a guarded alpha.1 fallback and stable empty-map fallback so only pending indicators hide while running/todos/token/ETA keep working; explains silent degradation via the shared-boundary blast radius (cosmetic indicator vs multi-plugin outage). Guarding useSessions is treated equivalently.

Proposes refresh-only verification (no host restart), checks both entries render together, and covers B's paste/remove path with A enabled; hygiene covers defensive destructuring, a local boundary per tenant, and per-entry host boundaries with a genuine nesting/visibility trade-off discussion.

caps.reason: The final remedy targets plugin A (the crashing tenant) and host boundary structure; plugin B is consistently treated as an innocent co-tenant needing no fix, and the rejected reinstall advice is only quoted as a failed experiment.
